questions.question: For one spin of a fair spinner with eight equal sectors numbered 1 to 8, the sample space S has:
The event 'landing on a multiple of three' on the 1-to-8 spinner contains:
A learner's calculation produces a probability of 1,3. What does the 0-to-1 scale say?
options: The event is more than certain
The answer is fine if converted to 130%
The answer is wrong — no probability can exceed 1, so the calculation contains an error
The answer should be rounded down to 1

questions.question: On the fair 1-to-8 spinner, P(multiple of three) is:
A bag holds 4 yellow, 5 purple and 3 orange marbles. P(purple) is:
options: 1/3, since purple is one of three colours

questions.question: From the same bag, P(yellow or orange) is:
Why is the denominator for the marble bag 12 and never 3?
options: Because the equally likely outcomes are the individual marbles, not the colours
Because probabilities must have even denominators
Because three colours would make the fraction improper

questions.question: A drawing pin is tossed 250 times and lands point-up 90 times. The relative frequency of point-up is:
Why can the drawing pin's probability not be found theoretically?
options: Drawing pins are too small to count
Its lopsided shape means point-up and point-down are not equally likely, so counting outcomes proves nothing
Theoretical probability only works for numbers, not objects

questions.question: As the number of trials grows from 10 to 250 to 2 500, the relative frequency:
options: settles toward a steady value — the estimate becomes more trustworthy

questions.question: A fair coin shows 33 heads in 60 tosses (0,55). A second coin shows 70% heads over 3 000 tosses. The correct judgement is:
options: The first coin is biased; the second is fine
The first is normal small-sample wobble; the second is strong evidence of a weighted coin

questions.question: On the 1-to-8 spinner, P(not landing on 8) is:
A forecast gives a 0,25 chance of rain tomorrow. The chance of a dry day is:
P(A) + P(not A) = 1 because A and its complement are:
options: mutually exclusive and exhaustive — they can never both occur, yet one of them must

questions.question: From the bag of 4 yellow, 5 purple and 3 orange marbles, P(not orange) computed two ways gives:
options: 1 − 3/12 = 3/4, confirmed by the 9 non-orange marbles out of 12

subtopics.title: A Scale From Impossible to Certain

questions.question: On the volume-slider picture of probability, 'the spinner shows a 9' sits:
Which event belongs exactly at the centre of the slider, at 0,5?
options: The spinner showing a number below nine

questions.question: The slider acts as an error alarm because:
options: it shows which events are most common
sliders are used in real laboratories
no event can sit left of 0 or right of 1, so any calculated value outside that range must be a mistake

subtopics.title: Counting Your Way to a Probability

questions.question: Twelve fruit gums: 4 yellow, 5 purple, 3 orange. Eyes shut, packet shaken — the chance of grabbing a purple one is:
The two questions that solve every fair-object problem are:
options: How heavy is each object, and how many are there?
How many could you grab, and how many of those would make you happy?
How many colours are there, and which is brightest?
How many trials were run, and how many succeeded?

questions.question: The 'count things, not types' warning means:
options: the equal candidates are the individual gums — purple holds 5 tickets in the draw, orange only 3 — so the denominator is 12
the denominator is the number of groups listed

questions.question: After 250 tosses of the drawing pin, 90 land point-up. Experience estimates P(point-up) as:
options: 0,5, because there are two ways to land

questions.question: Five tosses showing 3 point-ups is called 'a rumour, not evidence' because:
options: tiny samples wobble far from the true tendency — only large tallies settle near it
drawing pins behave differently in small groups
the first tosses of any experiment never count

questions.question: Which pairing of object and engine is correct?
options: Fair spinner: tally 250 spins; drawing pin: count sectors
Fair spinner: count and divide; drawing pin: gather data and divide occurrences by attempts
